# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**RE:** Appeal of adverse benefit determination
**Member:** Jordan Mercado
**Member ID:** W484245232
**Reference number:** POC-FD00FECEC4-98407
**Date of denial notice:** August 11, 2026
**Service at issue:** Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
**Plan:** Excellus BlueCross BlueShield (Commercial/ACA), New York

This appeal is submitted under the plan's governing clinical criteria, **eviCore CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty** (effective November 5, 2025), available at:
https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-07/EviCore_CMM-313%20Hip%20Replac%20Arthro_Final_V2.0.2025_eff11.05.2025_pub07.22.2025.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my total hip replacement (CPT 27130), which the plan denied on August 11, 2026. The notice states that the records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the records already submitted document the non-surgical care the plan's own criteria describe, and my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below, I have set the plan's published criteria next to what is in my chart.

## 1. The plan's conservative care requirement — and what my records show

The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration"

My records document the following provider-directed non-surgical management:

- **Supervised physical therapy, 12 weeks:** hip abductor strengthening and gait training, from April 4, 2026 through June 27, 2026, with 20 visits completed. This is recorded in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **NSAIDs for 6 months,** with inadequate relief.
- **Corticosteroid injection on April 3, 2026,** which gave only about two weeks of partial relief.

Taken together, this is more than three months of physician-directed non-surgical treatment, documented with dates, visit counts and outcomes. The denial reason given in my notice does not appear to be reconciled with these entries in the file, and I am asking the reviewer to look at them directly.

## 2. The plan's symptom criteria

The policy states:

> "Symptoms include BOTH of the following:"

> "function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall)for at least three (3) months duration"

> "loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"

My records show 14 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest. I walk with a cane and am limited to one block. I cannot put my own shoes on without help. My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

The plan's example in its own criteria describes limitation to two city blocks; my documented limit is one block, and my documented symptom duration is 14 months rather than three.

## 3. The plan's imaging criteria

The policy states:

> "Imaging shows ANY of the following findings:"

The excerpts I have of this section list, among other findings:

> "Tönnis Grade 2 - 3 osteoarthritis"

> "avascular necrosis with collapse of the femoral head"

> "inflammatory arthritis affecting BOTH the femoral head and the acetabulum with joint space narrowing"

My imaging of record is a weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph dated July 14, 2026, which shows the joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes.

I want to be straightforward here: my radiology report, as summarized in the packet, describes those findings but does not assign a grade, and I am not going to characterize it beyond what it says. The plan's imaging criterion is introduced by a colon and continues into a list that I have not been given in full. If the plan's decision rested on this section, I ask the plan to identify in writing which imaging criterion it applied and which element it considered unmet, so that my surgeon can respond to the specific point.

## 4. The policy's own exceptions, and the surgeon's role

The policy also states:

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of function-limiting pain is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate."

> "Criteria exception: Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate"

I am not relying on these exceptions, because my chart documents the full course of non-surgical care described above. I point them out only to show that the plan's criteria treat the three-month conservative care requirement as one that the medical record can satisfy in more than one way — and my record satisfies it directly.

The policy further states:

> "Note: It is incumbent on the surgeon to preoperatively optimize reasonably modifiable medical and behavioral health comorbidities."

On this point, my records document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

I should note that the criteria document also contains sections I have not been given in full, including headings the plan's criteria list such as "Femoral Head/Neck Fracture" and "Osteoarthritis, Avascular Necrosis (AVN), Inflammatory Arthritis." Where I have not quoted the plan's exact language above, I am arguing from my own records and not attributing any wording to the plan.

## What I am asking for

I ask the plan to overturn the denial and authorize CPT 27130. In the alternative, I ask that the plan:

1. Identify the specific criterion from eviCore CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty that it found unmet, and the records it reviewed in reaching that conclusion;
2. Confirm that the physical therapy discharge note dated through June 27, 2026, the NSAID course, and the April 3, 2026 injection record were part of the file reviewed; and
3. Provide the reviewing clinician's specialty, and make the file available to my surgeon for a peer-to-peer discussion.

I understand this appeal must be received by **February 7, 2027**, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and I understand I may also call the Customer Care number on my member card about this appeal.

I am glad to provide any additional records the plan needs. Please contact me if anything in my file is missing.

Thank you for reconsidering this decision.

Sincerely,

**Jordan Mercado**
Member ID: W484245232
